title: The present perfect: he hablado
summary: Talk about today, this week and life experience: he comido, has visto, hemos vuelto.
content:
## What the present perfect is for

The **pretérito perfecto** links the past to now. Use it for a period that is still open (**hoy**, **esta semana**, **este año**), for recent news and for life experience with no date attached.

- *Hoy he trabajado mucho.* (Today I have worked a lot.)
- *Esta semana hemos visto dos películas.* (This week we have seen two films.)
- *He estado en Japón.* (I have been to Japan.)

If the moment is closed (*ayer*, *el año pasado*), use the preterite instead: *Ayer trabajé mucho.*

> In Spain *hoy he comido* is normal for today. Most of Latin America says *hoy comí* and keeps the present perfect for experiences. Both are correct.

## Haber + participle

The tense has two pieces. The first is the present of **haber**, an auxiliary that never means *to have* in the sense of owning. The second is the **past participle**, which never changes.

| | haber | + participle |
|---|---|---|
| yo | **he** | hablado |
| tú | **has** | comido |
| él / ella / usted | **ha** | vivido |
| nosotros/as | **hemos** | hablado |
| vosotros/as | **habéis** | comido |
| ellos / ellas / ustedes | **han** | vivido |

Regular participles: **-ar** verbs take **-ado** (*hablar → hablado*), and **-er / -ir** verbs take **-ido** (*comer → comido*, *vivir → vivido*).

Nothing goes between haber and the participle. **No** and pronouns go **before haber**: *No lo he visto.* *Me he levantado tarde.* (Never *he me levantado*.)

## Irregular participles

A short list of very common verbs has its own participle. Learn them as a set.

| verb | participle | verb | participle |
|---|---|---|---|
| hacer | **hecho** | escribir | **escrito** |
| decir | **dicho** | abrir | **abierto** |
| ver | **visto** | volver | **vuelto** |
| poner | **puesto** | romper | **roto** |
| morir | **muerto** | | |

- *¿Qué has hecho hoy?* (What have you done today?)
- *No me han dicho nada.* (They haven't told me anything.)
- *¿Dónde has puesto las llaves?* (Where have you put the keys?)

Compounds follow suit: *describir → descrito*, *devolver → devuelto*.

## Ya, todavía no, alguna vez, nunca

Four small words often go with this tense.

- **ya** = already: *Ya he terminado.* (I have already finished.)
- **todavía no** = not yet: *Todavía no he desayunado.* (I haven't had breakfast yet.)
- **alguna vez** = ever (in questions): *¿Has estado alguna vez en Cuba?* (Have you ever been to Cuba?)
- **nunca** = never: *Nunca he comido paella.* or *No he comido nunca paella.*

A typical exchange: *¿Ya has visto la película?* (Have you seen the film yet?) *No, todavía no la he visto.* (No, I haven't seen it yet.)

vocabulary.meaning: to have (auxiliary verb for compound tenses)
vocabulary.example_meaning: Today I have eaten at home.
Today I have worked a lot.

vocabulary.example: Esta semana hemos visto dos películas.
vocabulary.example_meaning: This week we have seen two films.
I have already finished my homework.
Have you ever been to Japan?
Where have you put the keys?

vocabulary.example: Hemos escrito un correo al hotel.
vocabulary.example_meaning: We have written an email to the hotel.

vocabulary.example: Mis padres han vuelto de Galicia.
vocabulary.example_meaning: My parents have come back from Galicia.

quiz.explanation: Yo takes 'he' plus the participle: 'Hoy he trabajado mucho.' Haber is followed by the participle, not the infinitive.
hints: Haber is followed by a participle in -ado / -ido.

quiz.prompt: Conjugate in the present perfect: (nosotros) comer → ___
quiz.explanation: Nosotros takes 'hemos', and -er verbs form the participle in -ido: 'hemos comido'.
Tú takes 'has', and hacer has the irregular participle 'hecho': '¿Qué has hecho hoy?'

quiz.prompt: Complete with the present perfect of ver: Todavía no (yo) ___ la película.
quiz.explanation: 'Todavía no' (not yet) calls for the present perfect, and ver has the irregular participle 'visto': 'Todavía no he visto la película.'
hints: The participle of ver is irregular.

quiz.explanation: 'Alguna vez' asks about life experience, so the present perfect: 'has' + the participle 'estado'.

quiz.prompt: Complete with the present perfect of volver: Mis padres ___ de Galicia esta semana.
quiz.explanation: Mis padres means ellos, so the verb is 'han', and volver has the irregular participle 'vuelto': 'han vuelto'.
hints: The participle of volver is vuelto, not volvido.

quiz.prompt: Where does the pronoun go with he levantado? Pick the correct sentence.
quiz.explanation: Nothing can come between haber and the participle, and pronouns go before haber: 'Me he levantado tarde.'
hints: Where does the pronoun go: before haber, between, or after?

quiz.prompt: Complete with the present perfect of poner: ¿Dónde (tú) ___ las llaves?
quiz.explanation: Tú takes 'has', and poner has the irregular participle 'puesto': '¿Dónde has puesto las llaves?'
hints: The participle of poner is puesto.

quiz.explanation: Nosotros takes 'hemos', and escribir has the irregular participle 'escrito'. The participle never agrees with the subject after haber: 'Ya hemos escrito un correo.'
hints: The participle of escribir is escrito.

listening.note: New word: las gafas = the glasses.

listening.meaning: Have you already finished the work?

listening.text: Todavía no he leído el periódico.
listening.meaning: I haven't read the newspaper yet.
listening.note: New word: el periódico = the newspaper.

listening.meaning: Have you all ever been to Seville?

listening.text: Mi hermano ha roto la ventana de la cocina.
listening.meaning: My brother has broken the kitchen window.

listening.text: Esta semana he escrito dos correos a mi jefe.
listening.meaning: This week I have written two emails to my boss.

listening.text: No le he dicho nada porque todavía no he abierto la carta.
listening.meaning: I haven't told her anything because I haven't opened the letter yet.
listening.note: New word: la carta = the letter.

guide.section: What the present perfect is for

guide.tip: Say the nine irregular participles in a rhythm: hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto, vuelto, roto, muerto. Every other participle you need for now ends in -ado or -ido.

conversations.title: What have you done today?
conversations.scenario: Carmen phones Diego on a Monday evening to catch up on the day and make plans.

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Hi, Diego. What have you done today?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Pues he trabajado toda la mañana y por la tarde he ido al gimnasio. ¿Y tú?
lines.meaning: Well, I've worked all morning and in the afternoon I've been to the gym. And you?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Yo me he levantado tarde y todavía no he salido de casa.
lines.meaning: I got up late and I haven't left the house yet.
lines.note: The pronoun goes before haber. Also todavía no.

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: ¿Has visto la nueva película de Almodóvar? La ponen esta semana.
lines.meaning: Have you seen the new Almodóvar film? It's on this week.

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: No, todavía no la he visto. ¿Tú ya la has visto?
lines.meaning: No, I haven't seen it yet. Have you already seen it?

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, la he visto dos veces. ¡Es buenísima!
lines.meaning: Yes, I've seen it twice. It's really good!

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: ¿Has estado alguna vez en el cine Doré? Es muy bonito.
lines.meaning: Have you ever been to the Doré cinema? It's very pretty.

lines.speaker: b
lines.meaning: I've never been. Shall we go on Saturday?

lines.speaker: a
lines.text: Vale. Ah, ¿has hablado con Marta? Me ha dicho que ha vuelto de Galicia.
lines.meaning: OK. Oh, have you spoken to Marta? She told me she's back from Galicia.
lines.note: decir gives dicho, volver gives vuelto

lines.speaker: b
lines.text: Sí, me ha escrito un mensaje esta mañana. Ha roto el móvil en el viaje.
lines.meaning: Yes, she wrote me a message this morning. She broke her phone on the trip.
lines.note: escribir gives escrito, romper gives roto

lines.speaker: a
lines.meaning: Poor Marta! Well, see you on Saturday.

bites.title: Past, but touching now
bites.rule: Use haber plus a participle for things done in a period that is still open: hoy, esta semana, este año. A closed moment (ayer, el año pasado) takes the preterite.
bites.example_meaning: Today I have worked a lot.

bites.title: Two pieces together
bites.rule: Use he, has, ha, hemos, habéis or han plus a participle (-ado / -ido). Nothing goes between them. No and pronouns go before haber.
bites.example: No lo he visto. Me he levantado tarde.
bites.example_meaning: I haven't seen it. I got up late.

bites.title: The nine irregulars
bites.rule: Nine common participles do not end in -ado or -ido: hecho, dicho, visto, puesto, escrito, abierto, vuelto, roto, muerto.

bites.title: Ya or todavía no
bites.rule: Ya means already, todavía no means not yet, alguna vez means ever (in questions) and nunca means never. All four go with the present perfect.
bites.example_meaning: Have you eaten already? — Not yet.

sorts.title: Regular or irregular participle?
sorts.why: Most participles end in -ado or -ido. Hecho, visto, escrito and puesto belong to the short irregular list.

sorts.title: Which tense does the marker want?
sorts.why: Open periods (hoy, esta semana) and ya, todavía no and alguna vez take the present perfect. Closed moments (ayer, anoche, pasado/a) take the preterite.

sorts.title: Who has done it?
sorts.why: The person is in haber: he = yo, has = tú, ha = él/ella, han = ellos.

spots.why: Haber is followed by the participle, not the infinitive: he comido.
Hacer has the irregular participle hecho.

spots.sentence: Mis padres ha vuelto de Galicia.
spots.why: Mis padres = ellos, so han vuelto.
After haber comes the participle: estado.
Escribir has the irregular participle escrito.
The nosotros form of haber is hemos.

builds.meaning: Today I have worked a lot.
What have you done this week?

builds.text: Todavía no he visto la película.
builds.meaning: I haven't seen the film yet.
Have you ever been to Mexico?
